To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neural ensemble is the basic unit for the storage and retrieval of information about a stimulus, and that this ensemble consists of a large number of neurons with similar response patterns to the stimulus, which are changed in the absence of a correct behavioral response.
the average evoked responses of a neural ensemble in the brain are stable and reproducible and that the average pattern of response to a stimulus is changed when the animal fails to perform.
the conditioned stimulus elicits a burst of neuronal discharges that is followed by a late component of activity that is correlated with the correct performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the neural correlates of conditioned responses and the role of different brain regions and neuronal ensembles in learning.
the study of the neural basis of conditioned reflexes.
the neural correlates of conditioned responses and the neural mechanisms underlying the formation of memory traces in the brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the neural ensemble, as a unit, displays a pattern of response that is characteristic of the stimulus.

the average pattern of activity displayed by the aggregate of neurons is a reliable indicator of the information about a conditioned stimulus and that the late component in the average response is an indicator of the retrieval of the memory about the stimulus.
a conditioned response is represented by a pattern of neuronal discharges in an aggregate of brain neurons.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
conditioned stimuli are represented by stable patterns of activity in a distributed ensemble of neurons.
the neural ensemble is the basic unit of information processing.
the brain is not a computer, but a neural network.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the average pattern of response of the aggregate is a more reliable index of the representation of a stimulus than is any single unit.
we are able to record from multiple neurons in multiple regions of the brain at the same time, and we can use that data to make inferences about the neural mechanisms of memory.
we are able to record the activity of multiple single neurons simultaneously in awake, behaving animals.
